title: MemGuard: Persisting Verifier Signals for LLM-Agent Memory Governance

visual_explainer.blocker: No paper-grounded mechanism figure was available; the record remains text-only rather than publishing an unverified synthesis.

analysis.tldr: Persisting verifier descriptors across admission, retrieval, conflict handling, and archival beats a one-shot verifier filter in all reported means under matched runtime budgets, but the closest contrast lacks significance tests and the full gain is a multi-stage package.
analysis.problem: One-shot verification cannot prevent accepted-but-bad memories from remaining active or repair duplicate, stale, and conflicting state.
analysis.core_idea: Attach reward, confidence, label, and uncertainty to every memory and reuse those signals throughout its lifecycle.

memory_design.write: A verifier scores a candidate before activation.
memory_design.organize: Descriptors guide conflicts, merging, summarization, and archival.
memory_design.read: Precision-oriented retrieval and guard injection use persistent verifier metadata.
memory_design.update_forget: Maintenance revisits state using the same descriptors; deletion, privacy, and calibration drift are not audited.

compared_to: Verifier-only Filter under matched task order, steps, retrieval, and context budgets
Simplified label-plus-confidence descriptors and random/uniform weights
analysis.evidence: Across 16 backbone-benchmark settings and five seeds, full MemGuard is best on success and steps. For Qwen Plus, full versus verifier-only is 67.4/63.7, 83.6/79.8, 58.4/52.0, and 51.8/46.8. BH/Holm tests apply to ReasoningBank, not the verifier-only contrast.
analysis.why_it_matters: Verifier output becomes governed state only when it persists beyond admission and changes later maintenance and consumption.
limitations: Full versus verifier-only still bundles retrieval, conflict, merge, archival, and prompt changes, with no reported significance test for this closest contrast.
A simplified descriptor comes within 0.7–1.5 points and random/uniform weights are close, weakening fine-grained weighting claims.
Verifier/governance adds 4.0–5.8k tokens; dollars, energy, calibration, privacy, and delete costs are unreported.
